data.name: Module.diagnostic
data.value: Diagnostics

data.name: Diag.Bsod.Title
data.value: {0} blue screen(s) in the last 30 days

data.name: Diag.Bsod.Explanation.Driver
data.value: Usually caused by a faulty or outdated driver (graphics card, network, chipset). Updating drivers often fixes it.

data.name: Diag.Bsod.Explanation.Memory
data.value: Often linked to memory (RAM) or a driver that corrupts it. Test the memory with the Windows Memory Diagnostic.

data.name: Diag.Bsod.Explanation.Disk
data.value: Windows could not read the disk properly. Check disk health and back up your files.

data.name: Diag.Bsod.Explanation.Hardware
data.value: The hardware reported an error (processor, overheating, power supply). Check temperatures and cleanliness of the PC.

data.name: Diag.Bsod.Explanation.System
data.value: An essential Windows process stopped. Checking system files (repair below) can help.

data.name: Diag.Bsod.Explanation.Unknown
data.value: Windows stopped to protect itself. The technical details give the stop code.

data.name: Diag.Shutdowns.Title
data.value: {0} unexpected shutdowns in the last 30 days

data.name: Diag.Shutdowns.Explanation
data.value: The PC turned off without shutting down properly (power cut, power button held, power supply or overheating).

data.name: Diag.AppCrash.Title
data.value: "{0}" crashed {1} times in 30 days

data.name: Diag.AppCrash.Explanation
data.value: Updating or reinstalling this program usually fixes repeated crashes.

data.name: Diag.Device.Title
data.value: Device in error: {0} (code {1})

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.1
data.value: The device is not configured correctly. Reinstall its driver.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.3
data.value: The driver may be damaged, or the PC is low on memory. Reinstall the driver.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.10
data.value: The device cannot start. Update its driver or reconnect it.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.12
data.value: Not enough free resources for this device. Disable another device or update the BIOS.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.14
data.value: The device needs the PC to restart.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.18
data.value: Reinstall the driver of this device.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.19
data.value: Its configuration in the registry is damaged. Uninstall the device, then restart.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.21
data.value: Windows is removing this device. Restart the PC.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.24
data.value: The device is missing or not working. Check the connection.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.28
data.value: No driver is installed. Install it from Windows Update or the manufacturer's site.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.31
data.value: Windows cannot load the driver. Update it.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.32
data.value: A required driver is disabled.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.37
data.value: The driver failed to start. Reinstall it.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.39
data.value: The driver is missing or damaged. Reinstall it.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.43
data.value: Windows stopped the device because it reported a problem (often a hardware fault or a bad driver).

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.47
data.value: The device was prepared for safe removal. Unplug and plug it back.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.48
data.value: The driver is blocked because it causes problems. Get a newer version from the manufacturer.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.52
data.value: The driver signature cannot be verified. Install a signed driver from the manufacturer.

data.name: Diag.Device.Code.Other
data.value: The device reports an error. Updating or reinstalling its driver usually helps.

data.name: Diag.Disk.Title
data.value: Disk "{0}" shows signs of failure

data.name: Diag.Disk.Explanation.Warning
data.value: Windows reports that this disk is wearing out. Back up your files and plan to replace it.

data.name: Diag.Disk.Explanation.Critical
data.value: This disk is failing: back up your files now and replace it.

data.name: Diag.Reboot.Title
data.value: A restart is pending

data.name: Diag.Reboot.Explanation
data.value: Updates or installations will finish after a restart.

data.name: Diag.OldDrivers.Title
data.value: {0} driver(s) older than 5 years

data.name: Diag.OldDrivers.Explanation
data.value: Old drivers can cause instability. Look for updates on the manufacturer's site (automatic updates arrive in a later version).

data.name: Repair.FlushDns.Title
data.value: Clear the DNS cache

data.name: Repair.FlushDns.Explanation
data.value: Fixes websites that do not open while the Internet works. Instant and harmless.

data.name: Repair.SystemFiles.Title
data.value: Check Windows system files (SFC)

data.name: Repair.SystemFiles.Explanation
data.value: Finds and repairs damaged Windows files. Takes 10 to 30 minutes.

data.name: Repair.WindowsImage.Title
data.value: Repair the Windows image (DISM)

data.name: Repair.WindowsImage.Explanation
data.value: Downloads healthy copies of damaged components from Windows Update. Run it if SFC could not repair everything. Takes 10 to 40 minutes.

data.name: Help.Title
data.value: If Windows no longer starts

data.name: Help.Step1
data.value: 1. Turn the PC off and on three times in a row during startup: Windows then opens its recovery environment (blue screen "Choose an option").

data.name: Help.Step2
data.value: 2. Choose Troubleshoot > Advanced options > System Restore, and pick the restore point created by PCDoc before its last changes.

data.name: Help.Step3
data.value: 3. If that is not enough: Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Settings > Safe Mode, then undo the last changes from PCDoc's History page.

data.name: Help.Step4
data.value: 4. Last resort: Troubleshoot > Reset this PC > Keep my files.
